title: MS Teams processes bundled with Command Palette in Task Manager

status.label: Needs focused investigation
status.detail: Task Manager sometimes groups Teams and other applications launched via Command Palette under the Command Palette process.

next_action.label: Reproduce and review proposal
next_action.reason: Current launch paths use COM activation for packaged applications and shell execution for executables; the maintainer's earlier investigation did not establish a safe general solution.

judgment.rationale: Current launch paths use COM activation for packaged applications and shell execution for executables; the maintainer's earlier investigation did not establish a safe general solution.
evidence: The reporter observed the grouping disappear after a Teams update and later return.
A maintainer investigated and reported no consistent shell-equivalent launch method in May 2026.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the reported behavior and review the scoped proposal before implementation.

fix_assessment.rationale: Current launch paths use COM activation for packaged applications and shell execution for executables; the maintainer's earlier investigation did not establish a safe general solution.

proposed_fixes.title: Investigate shell-equivalent launch ownership and Task Manager grouping
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: the launch route or process-parent relationship leads Task Manager to group applications with Command Palette; Windows grouping behavior and packaged-app activation require verification.
plan: Reproduce the exact Teams launch path and capture process parentage before and after the grouping appears.
Compare shell and Command Palette launches for packaged and executable apps.
Only if a supported shell-equivalent route preserves launch semantics, adopt it and test both activation types.
verification: Teams and representative packaged and executable apps launch correctly and Task Manager grouping is verified without breaking elevation or arguments.

confidence.rationale: Current launch paths use COM activation for packaged applications and shell execution for executables; the maintainer's earlier investigation did not establish a safe general solution.

reproduce.title: Investigate shell-equivalent launch ownership and Task Manager grouping
setup: Close test Teams processes and start Command Palette.
steps: Launch Teams using Command Palette and inspect its process grouping and parentage.
Repeat launching the same app from the Windows shell.
Repeat after Teams restart or update and compare another packaged application.
reproduce.expected_result: The grouping and parentage differences are documented; launches retain normal arguments and behavior.
